active_paradigms.idea: Replace edge-count-only decoding with permutation-invariant noisy degree-profile MAP using bipartite assignment
active_paradigms.description: The current program has two modes: exact graph-edit-distance decoding only for N<=6, and otherwise a one-dimensional edge-count code. The latter discards almost all information surviving vertex shuffling: the multiset of N noisy vertex degrees is also invariant and provides roughly N observations instead of one. Construct each code graph with a deliberately distinct sorted degree sequence, for example by realizing graphical near-regular/two-level degree sequences whose degree histograms are well separated across message IDs. For a received graph, compute its sorted degree list dH. For each candidate codeword, form the likelihood cost of matching observed degree dH[a] to source degree dG[b], using the distribution Binomial(dG[b],1-eps)+Binomial(N-1-dG[b],eps), and solve the minimum-cost matching with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Sum the matched negative log likelihoods and choose the message of minimum cost; this is substantially more principled than comparing only expected total edge count. Tune N and the degree-sequence spacing against the actual score objective, approximately maximizing -log(N)+100*p_error*log(0.9), rather than selecting N from a fixed 2.5-sigma edge-count rule. This is especially valuable at moderate noise, where full vertex alignment is expensive or unreliable but degree information remains strongly usable.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primarily reduce the expected number E of wrong answers at the same or smaller N; because the score contains 0.9^E, even a small reduction in per-query error is usually worth a moderate increase in N.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not compare degree vectors positionwise after sorting without accounting for ambiguity among equal/near-equal degrees; assignment-based likelihood is the appropriate permutation-invariant decoder. Degrees are not fully independent because an edge contributes to two degrees, so use this as a robust pseudo-likelihood and validate it by simulation. Ensure every requested degree sequence is graphical and realize it deterministically; random realization is unnecessary. At eps=0, use exact degree matching and preferably supplement with a stronger invariant because many nonisomorphic graphs share a degree sequence.

active_paradigms.idea: Use spectral block-graph codes and decode from centered adjacency eigenvalues
active_paradigms.description: A fundamentally different code family is to encode each message as a deterministic block graph, such as a union/join of cliques or a small stochastic-block-style pattern blown up into blocks of carefully chosen sizes. Vertex shuffling leaves the adjacency spectrum unchanged, while independent edge flips perturb a structured adjacency matrix by a random matrix whose spectral norm is only about O(sqrt(N)). After receiving H, subtract the known noise baseline eps*(J-I), optionally project away the all-ones direction, and compute sorted eigenvalues with scipy.linalg.eigvalsh. Precompute the corresponding centered spectra for all code graphs and decode by a variance-weighted squared spectral distance, optionally retaining only the leading and trailing eigenvalues that carry the block signal. Varying block sizes and inter-block edge patterns gives many codewords whose signatures are global rather than merely total-edge differences. This can outperform both current branches for medium/high epsilon: unlike N<=6 GED it scales to useful N, and unlike edge count it uses several robust invariant coordinates. Choose the smallest N for which simulated spectral confusion is low enough to beat the denominator penalty, then use edge-count decoding only in regimes where spectral experiments show no gain.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exploit global structure that remains after arbitrary vertex permutation, reducing classification error for M up to 100 without requiring factorial graph matching.
active_paradigms.cautions: Raw adjacency spectra are dominated by the common mean density at high noise; centering by the known eps baseline and treating the principal all-ones component separately is essential. Avoid code graphs with repeated block sizes or cospectral constructions, since they create intrinsically ambiguous messages. Eigenvalue distance must be calibrated by noise level: leading eigenvalues have different variance from the bulk. Dense block graphs and their complements can be informative, but make sure candidate spectra remain separated after the factor (1-2*eps) shrinks the signal.

active_paradigms.idea: Select codewords jointly from a motif candidate pool with max-min integer programming instead of greedy GED or uniformly spaced edge counts
active_paradigms.description: The current GED branch greedily farthest-selects from all unlabeled graphs only up to six vertices, while the large-N branch fixes all messages on a single uniform edge-count line. Build a pool of candidate permutation-invariant code graphs at each plausible N: degree-profile graphs, clique-partition/block graphs, complements, and a small set of asymmetric regular-like graphs. For every candidate pair, estimate a confusion surrogate from the decoder feature distribution, such as squared Mahalanobis separation of edge count plus degree-histogram bins or spectral coordinates. Use scipy.optimize.milp with one binary variable per candidate and standard pairwise exclusion variables to select exactly M candidates while maximizing the minimum pair separation; candidates with low self-robustness can be excluded. Solve this independently for a small grid of N values and evaluate each resulting design by Monte Carlo using the same intended decoder. Rank designs by estimated expected official score (1/N times 0.9 raised to predicted errors across 100 queries), not merely by minimum distance. This jointly avoids crowded regions of invariant-feature space and is a direct replacement for the current arbitrary greedy ordering and fixed K_SEP threshold.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Optimize the entire M-codeword set for low mutual confusion and the actual exponential error penalty, while explicitly trading that against the 1/N denominator.
active_paradigms.cautions: Pairwise distance alone is only a surrogate for multiclass error, so include a few nearest competitors per codeword and validate the final selected pool by noisy simulation. The MILP can grow quadratically in pool size; keep a diverse, pruned pool rather than enumerating arbitrary graphs. Enforce that selected graphs are genuinely distinguishable under the chosen decoder, since identical degree/spectral feature vectors would otherwise be selected accidentally. The final implementation need not ship a Python solver: the optimized candidate tables/design rules can be generated offline and embedded, or a compact branch-and-bound equivalent can be implemented in C++.
